textbook.definition: A book used for learning a subject.

journal.definition: A daily written record of (usually personal) experiences and observations.

database.definition: An organized body of related information.

search-engine.definition: A service that finds webpages matching words that you type into a search box.
search-engine.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Search Engine" in an educational description.

bibliography.definition: A list of writings with time and place of publication (such as the writings of a single author or the works referred to in preparing a document etc.).

citation.definition: A short note recognizing a source of information or of a quoted passage.

footnote.definition: A printed note placed below the text on a printed page.

index.definition: A numerical scale used to compare variables with one another or with some reference number.

abstract.definition: Art that uses shapes, colours, or forms instead of realistic subjects.

peer-review.definition: A structured classroom exercise brings students together to read one another’s drafts and offer constructive feedback that improves the writing.

essay.definition: To put to the test, as for its quality, or give experimental use to.

thesis.definition: A treatise advancing a new point of view resulting from research.

dissertation.definition: A treatise advancing a new point of view resulting from research.

paper.definition: A thin flat material used for writing or drawing.

report.definition: A written document describing the findings of some individual or group.

literature-review.definition: A scholarly paper or section that examines and connects published studies about a particular subject.

methodology.definition: The branch of philosophy that analyzes the principles and procedures of inquiry in a particular discipline.

conclusion.definition: A position or opinion or judgment reached after consideration.

introduction.definition: The opening part of a report or study that presents its topic.

appendix.definition: Supplementary material that is collected and appended at the back of a book.

note-taking.definition: Related to or intended for writing down information during work, study, or other activities.

flashcard.definition: A card with words or numbers or pictures that is flashed to a class by the teacher.

mind-map.definition: To organize related ideas around a central thought in your mind, even without drawing them.

outline.definition: The outer line that shows the shape of something.

highlight.definition: A light area in a picture where light falls.

summarize.definition: To give the main points of something in a shorter form.

review.definition: An article that evaluates a book, film, product, or event.

memorize.definition: To learn something so that it can be recalled later.

practice-test.definition: Designed for practice tests that help students review material and develop effective ways to approach exams.

study-group.definition: A small, casual gathering lets students prepare together after class. Members exchange notes, explain difficult ideas, and review what they have learned.

plagiarism.definition: A piece of writing that has been copied from someone else and is presented as being your own work.

reference.definition: A short note recognizing a source of information or of a quoted passage.

original-work.definition: A book, artwork, or other creation made by its named author or artist rather than reproduced from another person's work.
original-work.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Original Work" in an educational description.

paraphrase.definition: Rewording for the purpose of clarification.

quote.definition: To repeat words spoken or written by someone else.

source.definition: A person, document, or place that provides information.

academic-honesty.definition: The principle of completing academic work truthfully, giving proper credit, and avoiding cheating, fabrication, or plagiarism.
academic-honesty.exampleUsage: The course begins with a discussion of academic honesty.

turnitin.definition: A brand of educational software used by institutions for assignment submission, text-similarity checking, and related academic-integrity workflows.
turnitin.exampleUsage: The university uses Turnitin as part of its academic-integrity process.

honor-code.definition: A school's official policy sets standards for student behavior, with special attention to honesty in assignments and exams.
